scope: Theorem 1, Proposition 2, and Corollary 3 for nondegenerate quadratic forms of positive dimension over arbitrary characteristic-zero fields.

proof_dependencies.claim: Existence and scalar compatibility of the trace
proof_dependencies.basis: Geometric transitivity, locally finite rational representations and Milne, Algebraic Groups, Section 12l and Theorem 22.42.

proof_dependencies.claim: Mathieu property in dimensions one and two
proof_dependencies.basis: Laurent torus characters and Duistermaat–van der Kallen's Newton-polytope criterion. A finitely generated coefficient field embeds in C. Eventual vanishing descends from the splitting field.

proof_dependencies.claim: Uniform all-order counterexample, sharp pure-power threshold for the displayed P, and geometric nonpower property
proof_dependencies.basis: Rotation recurrence checked summand by summand, scalar weight extraction, order 2k+1 endpoint divisibility, and simple zeros on the punctured x_1-axis. Long's normalizer calculation is the credited source of the endpoint method. The paper proves the argument on the quadratic complement.

proof_dependencies.claim: The complex cutoff is an instance of the reductive homogeneous-space classification
proof_dependencies.basis: Theorem 1.1 of Counterexamples to the Mathieu Property, applied to the stabilizer of a point for the SO(q) × G_m action. The proof of Theorem 1 does not need this previous classification.

blind_reader.supplied_context: Only the compiled PDF, the five questions in the paper guide, and a PDF-reading command. No access to repository files, earlier conversation, or web sources.

answers.contribution: All-field dimension cutoff, explicit original-field counterexamples in dimensions at least three, one fixed multiplier at every order, and absolute nonpower up to units.
answers.conceptual_reason: A rank-two splitting supplies the beta moments, scalar weights reduce the trace to one coefficient, and the endpoint identity puts the pure and marked coefficients on either side of the degree bound.
answers.hardest_step: Proposition 2 on pp. 3–4, where the endpoint error has order 2k+1. The rotation recurrence, coefficient bounds, and restriction argument were checked.
answers.limitations: Positive-dimensional nondegenerate forms in characteristic zero and this normalized trace. The low-dimensional direction uses the Laurent constant-term theorem.
answers.verification_obstacles: Imported results and historical priority require source inspection beyond the PDF. The first PDF could signal the algebraic closure more clearly and gave no visible repository locator for the pinned Long revision.

blind_reader.revisions: Spelled out the algebraic closure and the nonzero derivative on the punctured axis. Printed the GitHub repository and clickable revision. Made the Laurent weight bound explicit.
blind_reader.followup: The same isolated reader checked the revised PDF and its hash, confirmed that both issues were resolved, and reported no new ambiguity.
